02 · Skills Log

GW01

Group Work

During classroom activities, I worked with classmates to prepare shared tasks and contribute to group presentations. The photographs show a collaborative setting where participants held prepared notes and coordinated their roles. I supported the group by listening carefully, completing my responsibilities, and respecting different viewpoints. These experiences strengthened my cooperation, patience, reliability, confidence, and ability to achieve agreed outcomes together.

Linked evidenceFigures 2 and 4
TL02

Team Leading

I developed team-leading skills by helping organise responsibilities, encouraging participation, and keeping group activities focused. I learned to support classmates without dominating the task and to consider different opinions before decisions were made. Taking responsibility for progress improved my confidence and showed me that effective leadership requires fairness, responsibility, communication, accountability, patience, inclusion, encouragement, and willingness to help others succeed.

Linked evidenceFigures 2 and 4
AT03

Attendance

Regular attendance helped me follow lesson content, understand assessment requirements, and remain involved in classroom activities. Being present allowed me to receive instructions, ask questions, and contribute to group preparation. The presentation images provide evidence of participation in scheduled learning. I learned that dependable attendance supports continuity, confidence, responsibility, punctuality, preparation, engagement, professionalism, reliability, and stronger performance throughout the module.

Linked evidenceFigures 2 and 4
HW04

Hard Working

I demonstrated hard work by preparing for activities, reviewing instructions, and continuing with tasks when they required additional effort. I focused on completing work carefully instead of rushing and remained committed to group responsibilities. Preparing presentation material also required concentration and persistence. These experiences taught me that consistent effort, patience, self-discipline, resilience, and preparation improve the quality of academic work.

Linked evidenceFigures 2 and 4
CM05

Communication

My communication skills developed through classroom discussions, presentation preparation, and interaction with classmates. I practised explaining ideas clearly, listening attentively, and responding respectfully to other perspectives. Participating in a group presentation helped me organise information and communicate confidently. These experiences showed me that effective communication depends on clarity, preparation, active listening, empathy, professionalism, respect, and adapting messages to different situations.

04 · Reflection

Rolfe’s “What? So what? Now what?” model.

The reflective summary contains exactly 150 words and evaluates experience, learning and future action.

Exactly 150 wordsIndividual reflectionRolfe model
What?

What? Throughout this module, I developed group work, team leading, attendance, hard work, and communication through classroom activities, presentation preparation, and academic tasks. Working with classmates helped me understand how individual responsibility contributes to successful group outcomes.

So what?

So what? These experiences showed me that teamwork depends on reliability, respect, preparation, and clear communication. Regular attendance helped me follow instructions, receive feedback, and remain involved in group progress. I became more confident when contributing ideas, although I recognised that I can improve by speaking clearly and taking leadership responsibility earlier. I also learned that hard work requires persistence when tasks become challenging.

Now what?

Now what? I will prepare earlier, practise speaking from key points, and volunteer for responsibility in future projects. I will continue attending regularly and requesting constructive feedback. These actions will help me become a dependable team member, confident communicator, responsible leader, and effective professional in academic and workplace environments.

05 · Action Plan

Turning learning into future improvement.

Presentation confidence

Practise speaking from short prompts and request feedback on clarity, pace and delivery.

Leadership responsibility

Volunteer earlier for coordination roles while ensuring that every group member can contribute.

Consistent preparation

Break assessments into smaller weekly milestones and review progress before deadlines.

Harvard reference: Rolfe, G., Freshwater, D. and Jasper, M. (2001) Critical Reflection for Nursing and the Helping Professions: A User’s Guide. Basingstoke: Palgrave Macmillan.
